base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share: median of FY2023 $5.27, FY2024 $2.34, FY2025 $8.51 = $5.27/share. TTM override computed but rejected: FY25 OCF $5.452B - H1'25 $3.956B + H1'26 $1.299B = $2.795B, capex $1.118B, SBC $0.149B, TTM OE $1.528B = $3.15/share on 485M shares — H1'26 OCF is a working-capital build distortion (H1 net income $1.206B vs H1 OCF $1.299B). Latest FY $8.51 rejected as a working-capital release distortion.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 8.51 vs 3-yr median 5.27 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 4.9%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
moat_justification: Scale and hard-to-replicate origination/logistics/crush infrastructure and segment diversification, against no pricing power (price-taker on inputs and outputs), crush/ethanol margins set by commodity markets and EPA RVO policy, through-cycle ROIC in the high single digits (7.8% adjusted ROIC TTM at a cyclical upswing), and equally scaled undifferentiated rivals (Bunge, Cargill, COFCO).
name: Archer-Daniels-Midland Company
one_liner: Enduring commodity processor with scale/logistics advantages but no pricing power, moat 4/10 — at $80.42 (15.3x normalized OE of $5.27/share, after the RVO-driven guidance raise was priced in) it yields a 9.1% weighted IRR with IV@15% of $42.33; it clears the 15% hurdle only at ~$42 (~$34 with a margin of safety), and even the super-bull case stays below today's price.
